20. The Principal-Agent Problem

What does a contract look like when effort is unobservable — find the optimal performance pay where incentive compatibility meets participation, then decide whether the incentives are worth buying.

  • Moral Hazard and Incentives — When effort is unobservable, a flat wage invites shirking. The optimal contract (wL,wH)(w_L, w_H)(wL​,wH​) is where incentive compatibility (p1−p0)(uH−uL)=c(p_1 - p_0)(u_H - u_L) = c(p1​−p0​)(uH​−uL​)=c meets the participation constraint. Raise risk tolerance α\alphaα and the pay-for-performance slope flattens — the risk-sharing versus incentives tradeoff, made visible.
  • Which Effort to Implement — Incentivizing high effort has a price. Profit Π1(c)\Pi_1(c)Π1​(c) falls as the effort cost ccc rises, while low-effort profit Π0\Pi_0Π0​ stays flat. Buying incentives pays only left of the crossing c∗c^*c∗ — incentives are worth it only while the effort cost, hence the risk premium, is small enough.
